summary: Yasuo Yuasa worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1973) under Tetsuro Watsuji, later serving there (~1952–1958), at the University of Yamanashi (~1958–1967), Osaka University (1975), and the University of Tsukuba (1981–1989).

Yasuro Abe specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University (~1972–1976) and Otani University (~1976–1981). His main positions include Nagoya University (assistant professor 1994, professor 1998, professor emeritus 2000–2019) and Ryukoku University (professor 2019).

Yasusaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1895–1899) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyushu University (~1906–1928).
Yasushi Endo is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004), and Shitennoji University as professor (attested 2000).

Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and the University of Leipzig (attested 2015), and a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2016–2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1961–1970) and held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1979–2007), the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies as president (~2003–2007), and Koyasan University (~2007–2013).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yelena Rudenko works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, the University of Delhi, and R. B. Suleimenov Institute of Oriental Studies (PhD 2006–2009), where she also served as a research fellow (2006–2019).
Yellava Subbarayalu works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).
Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held posts at Middlebury College and as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia.

Yeshi Donden worked in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, where he served as director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2001).

Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hsing Yun, earned degrees at National Taiwan University and University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and completed a PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein (~1991–1996). She held posts at University of the West (~1996–2002) and Harvard (2001–2002).
Yifan Zhang is active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, serving as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Yigal Bronner specializes in Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–1999) under Sheldon Pollock, later becoming an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2013).

Yijie Tang worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1947–1951) and later served as a professor there (~1956–2014), as well as holding a post at Stanford University (~1990–1991).

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University under Yinke Chen (~1935–1939), and Harvard University (~1939–1944), later serving as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).
Yiling Hua works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Waseda University (2020–2024) and took up a lecturing post at Kunming University of Science and Technology in 2024.

Ying-Kuang Chu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1905–1907) and under traditional teachers including Nordan Hutuktu (1926), Bai Puren (1929), Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche.

Ying-shih Yü specialized in sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy, completing a PhD at Harvard (1955–1962). He held major professorships at Harvard (1969), Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton (1987–2001), and served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1973–1975).
